extra.message: User-controlled input request.POST['user_id'] (user_id_form) is concatenated via string formatting directly into a raw SQL query passed to User.objects.raw(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. via the user_id field), allowing data exfiltration or authentication bypass (the ORDER BY is_admin trick surfaces admin records).

hits_by_ip() builds a SQL string with Python string formatting using attacker-controlled 'ip' value and 'col' (column list), then executes it via cursor.execute(). Both 'ip' and the column names come from request.GET in admin_analytics (app/views/admin/views.py:88-98) with no sanitization, enabling SQL injection.

os.system() executes a shell command built with string formatting that includes the uploaded file's name (orig_file.name) which is fully attacker-controlled. A crafted filename (e.g. containing ';', '$()', or backticks) results in arbitrary OS command execution. Reached via the upload view (app/views/users/benefit_forms/views.py:43) with backup='true'.

eval() is called on the unvalidated 'class' GET parameter (classname = request.GET.get('class')). This allows arbitrary Python code execution, e.g. ?class=__import__('os').system('...'). The endpoint also has no authentication decorator, making it remotely exploitable.
eval() is called on the unvalidated 'class' GET parameter in api_id(). This permits arbitrary Python code execution from a remote, unauthenticated user via the ?class= parameter.

pickle.loads() is called on base64-decoded data taken directly from request.POST['user']. Deserializing attacker-controlled pickle data leads to arbitrary code execution (insecure deserialization). The endpoint requires no token/authentication for this POST.

The 'name' GET parameter is concatenated directly to BASE_DIR and opened as a file with no path sanitization, allowing path traversal (e.g. ?name=../../../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files on the server, which are then returned to the user.

The 'path' POST parameter is used directly as the redirect target in HttpResponseRedirect(path) with no validation. An attacker can supply an external URL to redirect the user after login (open redirect), enabling phishing.

safe_name() wraps the user-controlled first_name field in mark_safe(), disabling Django auto-escaping. It is rendered in template/layouts/shared/nav_loggedin.html as {{ current_user.safe_name }}, allowing stored XSS via the first_name field set at signup/update.

creator_name() returns safestring.mark_safe('Name unavailable'). While this literal is static, the pattern marks message-related output as safe and is rendered unescaped ({{ message.creator_name }}) in users/messages templates. Combined with mark_safe usage on user-derived names this disables escaping for message author display.

The mobile API api_index endpoint has no authentication decorator and serializes/returns all rows of an arbitrary model (selected via the 'class' parameter). Any unauthenticated user can dump sensitive data (e.g. User records including password hashes and tokens).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: user_work_info_index fetches the User by the user_id from the URL (User.objects.get(id=user_id)) instead of the authenticated user, and renders that user's work info (income, SSN, DoB). The user_is_authenticated decorator only checks login, not ownership, so any authenticated user can view another user's sensitive work info by changing the URL (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: admin_update_user (and the other admin_* views) are protected only by user_is_authenticated, with no check that the requester is an admin. Any logged-in user can update/delete/list arbitrary users (including changing passwords or escalating is_admin via the **data update), constituting broken access control / privilege escalation.

admin_analytics has no admin authorization check (only user_is_authenticated) and passes raw user GET input (ip and column names) into the SQL-building Analytics.hits_by_ip, exposing both broken access control and SQL injection to any authenticated user.
Django SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source. Exposure of the secret key allows forging signed cookies/sessions, password reset tokens, and CSRF tokens.

The AES encryption KEY and ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT (line 135) used to encrypt sensitive data (bank account numbers, SSNs) and validate API tokens are hardcoded in source. Anyone with source access can decrypt sensitive data or forge API tokens.

DEBUG = True is set. In production this exposes detailed stack traces, settings, and environment data on errors (information disclosure). Combined with ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*'] (line 27) this is a security misconfiguration.
Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (hashlib.md5) for authentication and storage. MD5 is fast and broken, making offline brute-force/rainbow-table attacks trivial if the database is compromised.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: Password reset tokens are generated as 'user_id-MD5(email)'. Since the email is often known/guessable and MD5 is unkeyed, an attacker can forge a valid reset token for any user and take over the account (predictable security token).

check_if_valid_token uses a weak/broken regex (.*?)-(.*) and SHA1 of ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT:group_id to validate tokens, and extrapolate_user derives the user_id from the token's id portion. The token only authenticates the id segment, allowing an attacker who learns one valid token to manipulate the id/hash split and impersonate other users or escalate to admin (improper authentication).

user_pay deletes a Pay record by pay_id from the URL (Pay.objects.get(id=pay_id).delete()) without verifying it belongs to the authenticated user. Any logged-in user can delete another user's direct-deposit/pay records (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: user_message fetches and deletes/views a Message by message_id (Message.objects.get(pk=message_id)) without checking that the authenticated current_user is the creator or receiver. Any logged-in user can read or delete arbitrary messages by guessing the id (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
